evidence: The code shape the finding describes exists: find_signal_implementation_run (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:481-516) calls webhooks.find_task_run (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-69, no team filter) and then returns None on the raw check `run.team_id != team_id` (api.py:504-505); the webhook carve-out passes team_id=repo_config.team_id (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:189-199) after resolving the config unscoped by installation+repo (tasks.py:292-306); StamphogRepoConfig is a ProductTeamModel (products/stamphog/backend/models.py:24) whose save() rewrites team_id via resolve_effective_team_id (posthog/models/scoping/product_mixin.py:86-96), which returns `team.parent_team_id or team_id` (posthog/models/scoping/manager.py:41-59); Task (products/tasks/backend/models.py:112,145), TaskRun (:1063,1079), SignalReport (products/signals/backend/models.py:184,201) and SignalReportArtefact (:693,745) are plain models with raw team FKs and no canonicalization; and the receiver leg does canonicalize because process_inbox_pr_review uses StamphogRepoConfig.objects.for_team(team_id) (tasks.py:1110-1131; for_team resolves canonical at manager.py:118-131) with the raw TaskRun team from receivers.py:126-140. So IF a child environment owned the run, the initial review would land and later pushes would hit the skip path that dismisses the standing approval without a replacement (tasks.py:870-905). The refutation is that no production call path in this tree can produce such a run: the divergence needs a Team with non-null parent_team_id, and nothing writes that column. Team.parent_team (posthog/models/team/team.py:306-312) is added by posthog/migrations/0705_team_parent_team.py as ADD COLUMN + CREATE INDEX with no backfill; TeamManager.create/create_with_data (team.py:94-135,176-192) never set it; TeamSerializer.create (posthog/api/team.py:1492-1512) forwards only validated fields plus project_id; multi-environment creation is disabled outright (ProjectEnvironmentsViewSet.initial raises PermissionDenied 'Multiple environments per project are no longer available', api/team.py:2424-2429; PremiumMultiEnvironmentPermission enforces one non-demo team per project, :2538-2560); the Django admin exposes parent_team in no fieldset or readonly list (posthog/admin/admins/team_admin.py:137-160,170-300; its only references are the clean_* guard at :100-103). A tree-wide grep for `parent_team=` / `parent_team_id=` writers finds only tests (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:107, products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_api.py:97,112, posthog/models/scoping/test_manager.py:129). With parent_team_id always null, resolve_effective_team_id(x) == x, repo_config.team_id equals the raw id the config was created under (tasks.py:666 `for_team(team_id).create(team_id=team_id)`; sync endpoint canonical_team_id at products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:163-172), and the raw comparison at api.py:505 is already the canonical comparison the finding asks for. The suggested SignalImplementationRunDTO source-environment field is likewise redundant today: resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:150-157) filters SignalReportArtefact by the same id (receivers.py:180-188). The remaining asks (add resolve_effective_team_id, add a child-environment regression test) are defensive hardening against a state the tree cannot reach.
notes: The verdict flips to should_fix the moment anything populates Team.parent_team_id in production: a backfill from project_id for legacy multi-environment teams, re-enabling environment creation with parent_team set, or exposing the field in admin. The scoping framework, stamphog views, review_hog views/tests and the signals scout fleet already canonicalize as if child environments were live, so this latent asymmetry is worth tracking; but I could not verify production data from the tree, and an out-of-tree backfill would make the finding real. I would also downgrade further if signal-report Task creation were shown to always use the canonical team, which would remove the mismatch even with child environments present.
